title: Latency attribution candidate harvester for per-request inference telemetry
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We need a low-cost, high-signal way to attribute tail latency and error spikes back to request-level attributes (tenant, route, model-variant, batching context) without flooding storage or increasing p99 for all requests. Goal: implement a lightweight 'candidate harvester' component that deterministically selects a bounded set of high-latency / error request candidates, attaches enriched context (trace-id, route, tenant, model version, kv-cache hit/miss flags, batch size), and exports a compact sample record for downstream analysis and dashboard exemplars. Non-goals: this ticket does not replace full distributed tracing or increase default sampling for all traffic. It does not include UI work past dashboard wiring.
approach: Run a small harvester process colocated with inference worker (sidecar or in-process hook). For each request, compute a deterministic candidate score using (request_id hash xor tenant_salt) combined with latency band thresholds. The harvester keeps a per-tenant sliding window counter and budget (e.g., 10 candidates / minute / tenant) and only retains requests that either exceed a latency threshold (configurable p95/p99 heuristics) or return a non-2xx error. For selected candidates we capture a compact manifest: trace_id, span_id (if present), route, model, quantization profile, batch size, kv-cache metadata, truncated prompt fingerprint, time-to-first-token, total-serve-ms, node-id, and a privacy-safe prompt hash. Export path: push manifests as OTLP traces with a dedicated attribute namespace and produce a minimal JSON record into the telemetry-compact Kafka topic for offline correlation. Also add exemplar attachment to the histogram exporter so Prometheus/OpenMetrics can link exemplars to trace ids.
instrumentation_details:
- Integration points: inference handler entry/exit, rpc layer (gRPC/http), kv-cache callbacks (hit/miss), batching scheduler hooks.
- Deterministic sampler: FNV-1a on request_id + tenant salt with configurable threshold to control sample rate.
- Memory: bounded ring buffer per tenant with LRU eviction.
- Export: produce OTLP span with "candidate.harvester" attribute and send JSON manifest to telemetry-compact topic.
- Security: redact any high-entropy user content, store only reversible metadata where necessary and maintain encryption at rest for the compact topic.
- Backpressure: if telemetry-compact topic is unavailable, fall back to local disk circular buffer and exponential backoff uploader.
acceptance_criteria: Harvester compiles and runs in dev environment with feature flag off by default
End-to-end pipeline delivers candidate manifests to telemetry-compact topic under normal load without increasing p99 by > 2% CPU or latency budget
Prometheus histogram receives exemplars with trace_id attribute for sampled tail requests
Dashboards display sample-linked traces for top-5 routes and allow clicking through to trace view
Security review sign-off on redaction rules and storage encryption
implementation_steps: Design proto for compact manifest and OTLP attribute namespace (contrib: @observability) - 1 day
Implement in-process hook and lightweight sidecar shim with deterministic sampler - 3 days
Add exporter to produce manifest to telemetry-compact Kafka topic and attach exemplars to histogram exporter - 2 days
E2E tests: synthetic traffic to validate sampling rates and exemplar linkage - 2 days
Canary rollout to us-west1 with monitoring and kill-switch feature flag - 1 day
Create dashboard panels and update runbook for tail-latency investigation - 1 day
risks_mitigation: Risk: Harvester increases CPU on inference nodes. Mitigation: keep code in sidecar, cap per-node CPU usage to 2% and gate sampling behind config.
Risk: PII leakage in compact manifests. Mitigation: implement strict redaction and store only stable prompt fingerprint; require security review before enabling for customer data.
Risk: Kafka topic backpressure. Mitigation: local circular buffer with TTL and backoff uploader; metrics to alert on dropped manifests.

Risk: Misattribution due to missing trace id. Mitigation: fallback to request_id -> create synthetic span linking to agent-collected logs and annotate as 'synthetic-link' for downstream tooling to surface.
Risk: tenant overload. Mitigation: per-tenant budgets and global throttle with quota-first policy.
